page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for graphics-intensive and machine learning workloads. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) operating at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, and 900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between CPU-only and GPU-accelerated tasks. Single-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% in stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and general operations like database tasks and web serving sit in the average range (middle 50%). However, the instance excels in GPU-driven workloads; LLM inference for small and medium models achieves top-tier performance, with prompt processing for a 7B model reaching 1173.99 tokens/second and text generation reaching 43.96 tokens/second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4dn.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density for workloads that can leverage both local NVMe storage and hardware acceleration without requiring top-tier CPU compute. The inclusion of a dedicated T4 GPU and 900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes it highly suitable for machine learning inference, small-to-medium LLM deployment, graphics rendering, and video transcoding. It is less optimal for single-threaded CPU-bound applications.
